about: Case file CF1 (cf1-supply-chain-microgrids). Research text: the texts of the 'study' and 'event' timeline steps and 'boundary' (its lists) are approved excerpt sentences (E8.13-E8.16), word for word; _tests/learn/test_cf1-supply-chain-microgrids.js checks them. Study dates are the publishers' dates on Crossref and the article PDF (accessed 3 Nov 2026); the code release date is GitHub's. 'idea' is an illustrative toy with invented round numbers in 2025 dollars, not the studies' inputs or results; its wind and sun take the shapes of SPP's 2025 hourly wind and solar (assets/learn/data/town_year.json, EIA-930), scaled to each site's capacity factor with LX.townProfile (method 'scale').

events.label: Journal article (this case)
events.text: Factories, warehouses and their on-site microgrids are sited and sized together, for a three-tier supply chain over one year; published online in February 2023, in the July 2023 issue.

source.label: Li et al. (2023), Applied Mathematical Modelling 119, 119–136

events.label: Conference paper
events.text: A two-tier version locates warehouses and sizes their microgrids, with electric-truck routing and electricity trading.

events.label: Code released
events.text: A documented, runnable implementation of the location models, with synthetic examples (version 1.0.1).

boundary.title: Where the result holds
holds: stylized supply-chain networks with synthetic distances and costs;
candidate sites in California, Arizona and Nevada;
products planned week by week and energy hour by hour over one year;
the modeled time-of-use tariffs and grid buying and selling prices.
leaves: grid outages, which the studies do not model;
real distances and costs, which are synthetic.
boundary.source: From Li et al. (2023), Applied Mathematical Modelling.

idea.title: One factory, two sites
idea.note: Illustrative numbers, not the studies' inputs or results.
